sampling_model.design: Independent observations from \(P_Q\), with a deterministic three-way sample split and known uniform covariate design on \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\).
sampling_model.treatment: Binary observational treatment with conditional ignorability and \(\kappa\le\pi_Q(x)\le1-\kappa\).
sampling_model.overlap: Uniform overlap is fixed over \(\mathcal X\); the full class also has a positive density band around \(x_0\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Private tensor-spline sufficient-statistic releases for \(\pi_Q\) and \(\mu_{0,Q}\), followed by Hölder-ball projection; a separate block supplies the privatized linear and quadratic local moments.
sampling_model.privacy: Replacement \((\epsilon_n,\delta_n)\)-differential privacy under parallel composition across disjoint blocks, a single joint Gaussian release within each block, and post-processing for stabilization and interval formation.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The higher-order local-polynomial learner attains the privacy-free pointwise CATE minimax rate under its regularity conditions.
Worst-case bias-aware local-polynomial confidence intervals are honest and shrink at the optimal nonparametric rate.
A doubly robust uniform confidence band is constructed for a lower-dimensional CATE function under nonprivate sampling.
DP-CATE preserves Neyman orthogonality asymptotically and gives quasi-oracle conditions for private two-stage CATE learners.
Theorem 4.6 constructs a valid private interval for the population ATE from private point and variance estimates.
A black-box resampling framework converts a private estimator into an asymptotically valid and tight nonparametric confidence interval.

body.tldr: The project constructs a replacement-private, finite-sample honest confidence interval for pointwise CATE on a concrete uniform-design, positive-density KBRW-attainable submodel. A fully private higher-order local learner uses projected private spline pilots and one joint Gaussian release of its localized linear and quadratic moments. The interval radius displays three separate contributions: Hölder localization plus higher-order nuisance bias, sampling fluctuation, and propagated privacy noise. Deterministic tuning yields an expected-length upper phase with the privacy-free KBRW term, an ordinary \(\gamma\)-smooth private-regression term, and a global-sensitivity higher-order term. On the unchanged full positive-density class, only the sound ordinary regression lower limitation is asserted; the exact nuisance-sensitive private confidence modulus remains open.

project_justification.gap: Private CATE papers provide point releases or quasi-oracle guarantees, and private causal interval papers treat regular average effects. They do not give a uniform pointwise Hölder CATE coverage theorem that accounts simultaneously for higher-order nuisance bias, sampling uncertainty, privacy composition, and privacy noise.
project_justification.niche: A bias-aware fixed-length construction on a fixed KBRW-attainable positive-density submodel permits honest nonregular causal inference without assuming the desired coverage or length and without relying on the rejected paired-microcell lower bound.
project_justification.fill: The project privatizes every pilot and localized moment under a blockwise accountant, proves a uniform finite-sample remainder inequality, derives a phase-sensitive expected-length upper bound, and separates it from an ordinary full-class lower limitation and an explicit sharpness question.

body.related_work: Kennedy, Balakrishnan, Robins, and Wasserman (2024) provide the privacy-free pointwise CATE minimax rate and the higher-order local-polynomial learner whose bias and variance architecture is retained here. Robins, Li, Tchetgen Tchetgen, and van der Vaart (2008) supply the higher-order influence-function perspective behind the quadratic correction. Armstrong and Kolesár (2020) motivate honest fixed-length intervals that expose worst-case smoothing bias rather than estimating it. Lee, Okui, and Whang (2017) obtain nonprivate doubly robust CATE confidence bands in a lower-dimensional heterogeneity problem. Schröder, Melnychuk, and Feuerriegel (2025) establish private Neyman-orthogonal CATE learning and explicitly identify privatization-induced uncertainty as unresolved, but do not derive a pointwise Hölder coverage or length phase. Schröder, Hartenstein, and Feuerriegel (2025) construct private intervals for the regular population ATE; their influence-function variance calculation does not cover localized higher-order CATE bias. Shoham, Shenfeld, Velner-Harris, and Ligett (2026) give a general asymptotic resampling conversion from private estimators to intervals; the present target instead requires uniform finite-sample Hölder bias control and an explicit expected-length phase. Dwork and Roth (2014) supply the Gaussian mechanism, parallel composition, and post-processing facts used by the privacy accountant.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The displayed higher-order privacy term comes from the global sensitivity \(m^{-1}(h^{-d}+k h^{-2d})\) of a direct clipped quadratic-moment release. It is an attainable upper-bound cost, not a minimax lower bound. The proposal does not revive the invalid \(q<\gamma\) paired-microcell transport construction and does not claim that this term is unavoidable on \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}\).
body.honest_scope: Settled targets are the construction, replacement-privacy accountant, uniform bias and concentration envelope, honest coverage, attainable-submodel expected-length upper phase, privacy-free reduction, and ordinary full-class regression lower limitation. The exact full-class minimax expected-length frontier, including whether higher-order nuisance privacy creates an additional unavoidable branch, is the open-ended question.
